newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down on arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down on arbitrage play.

text.p: * Volume rises to $165.60 million from $112.5 million
Arbitrage play for the weekend sent the Philippine peso lower at the close to 26.343 on Friday from the previous day's 26.340.
Traders said banks were selling dollars for same-day delivery to have the pesos that earn higher interest for the weekend. At the same time, banks bought the dollars they shorted for Monday-delivery.
The peso averaged at 26.341 for the day from 26.338.
Dealers said the Central Bank contained the movement of the peso. It intervened on both sides - buying and selling dollars.
A dealer said the Central Bank bought and sold dollars for same-day delivery at 26.337/26.34. It also purchased dollars at 26.344 for Monday-delivery.
The Central Bank's purchases totalled $24.5 million and sales at $10 million, the dealer said.
On Monday, dealers said the peso would just trade sideways. Oil firms would buy $13.5 million which is not likely to impact on the peso, they said.
